If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $x=\frac{1}{8}{y}^{3},\,$ $x=3-y,$ and $y=0,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type II region. To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154225/assets/2dcc8a77fea8a9fd3e95022edcd86e0a040c54fd30d88a7931c0542fdeaefd0b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\frac{1}{8}{y}^{3}\le x\le 3-y\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{y}^{3}/8}^{3-y}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{{y}^{3}/8}^{3-y}f(x,y)\,dx]dy\end{aligned}
$$
